content: 1. Recommendations for a public health approach to effective communication strategies were outlined in a document accessed on March 6, 2017. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a statement on the prevention and elimination of disrespect and abuse during facility-based childbirth, accessed on March 6, 2017. 3. A toolbox for examining laws, regulations, and policies related to reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health and human rights was made available, accessed on March 6, 2017. 4. An interagency statement addressing the elimination of forced, coercive, and involuntary sterilization was published by OHCHR, UN Women, UNAIDS, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, and WHO, accessed on March 6, 2017. 5. WHO provided guidance and recommendations to ensure human rights in the provision of contraceptive information and services, accessed on March 6, 2017. 6. WHO also published an implementation guide to ensure human rights within contraceptive service delivery, accessed on March 6, 2017. 7. A human rights analysis of existing quantitative indicators within contraceptive programs was conducted by WHO, accessed on March 6, 2017. 8. The second edition of WHO's technical and policy guidance for safe abortion within health systems was accessed on February 28, 2017. 9. Legal and policy considerations for safe abortion were outlined in a WHO document accessed on March 6, 2017. 10. A summary reflection guide on a human rights-based approach to health, focusing on sexual and reproductive health, maternal health, and under-5 child health for health workers, was published by OHCHR, Harvard FXB Center, PMNCH, UNFPA, and WHO, accessed on March 6, 2017. 11. A similar guide targeting health policymakers was also published by the same organizations, accessed on March 6, 2017. 12. Another guide for national human rights institutions on applying a human rights-based approach to health was made available, accessed on March 6, 2017. 13. A global survey on the sexual and reproductive health and human rights of women living with HIV was conducted, with key findings published by the Salamander Trust, accessed on March 6, 2017. 14. A systematic review of the mental health of people living with HIV in China from 1998 to 2014 was published in PLoS One in 2016. 15. Gender differences and psychosocial factors associated with quality of life among ART initiators in Oromia, Ethiopia, were studied and published in AIDS Behavior in 2016. 16. A global survey explored the impact of living with HIV on women's mental health, with findings published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2015. 17. WHO published recommendations on optimizing health worker roles to improve access to maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting, accessed on March 6, 2017. 18. WHO's Mental Health Action Plan for 2013–2020 was accessed on March 6, 2017. 19. The World Report on Violence and Health, published by WHO, was accessed on March 6, 2017. 20. A pressing need to address the sexual and reproductive health problems of adolescent girls living with HIV in lowand middle-income countries was highlighted in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2015. 21. A framework for creating an enabling environment for adolescent sexual and reproductive health was published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2015. 22. Access to medical care for adolescents was studied in the 1997 Commonwealth Fund Survey, with findings published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 1999. 23. WHO provided guidance for HIV testing, counseling, and care for adolescents living with HIV, accessed on March 6, 2017. 24. A reproductive health strategy to accelerate progress toward international development goals was adopted by the 57th World Health Assembly, accessed on March 6, 2017. 25. Additional sources of support for adolescent HIV testing, counseling, and care were outlined in an implementation guidance document, accessed on March 6, 2017. 26. WHO guidelines on preventing early pregnancy and poor reproductive outcomes among adolescents in developing countries were accessed on March 6, 2017. 27. A systematic review on food insecurity, sexual risk behavior, and adherence to antiretroviral therapy among women living with HIV was conducted, with findings under review in 2017. 28. WHO and UNAIDS published a guidance note on HIV and social protection, accessed on March 6, 2017. 29. A background paper on integrating sexual and reproductive health services with HIV interventions was presented at the 26th UNAIDS Programme Coordinating Board Meeting, accessed on March 6, 2017. 30. A rapid assessment tool for linking sexual and reproductive health and HIV services was made available, accessed on March 6, 2017. 31. A strategic framework for preventing HIV and unintended pregnancies from 2011–2015 was published, accessed on March 6, 2017. 32. A systematic review on integrating family planning services into HIV care and treatment services was conducted, with findings published in Studies in Family Planning in 2017. 33. WHO guidelines on preventing violence against women and responding to intimate partner violence were accessed on March 6, 2017. 34. A systematic review of interventions to reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination from 2002 to 2013 was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2013. 35. WHO and UNODC published guidelines for medico-legal care for victims of sexual violence, accessed on March 6, 2017. 36. A systematic review on the impact of HIV-related stigma on treatment adherence was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2013. 37. Joint WHO/ILO policy guidelines on improving health worker access to prevention, treatment, and care services for HIV and TB were accessed on March 6, 2017. 38. UNFPA operational guidance for comprehensive sexuality education with a focus on human rights and gender was accessed on January 31, 2017. 39. WHO recommendations for preventing and treating HIV and other sexually transmitted infections among sex workers in lowand middle-income countries were accessed on March 6, 2017. 40. UNAIDS published a global report on the AIDS epidemic in 2013, accessed on March 6, 2017. 41. A background document on the criminalization of HIV non-disclosure, exposure, and transmission was prepared for an expert meeting in Geneva, accessed on March 2, 2017. 42. General Comment No. 20 on non-discrimination in economic, social, and cultural rights was published, accessed on March 6, 2017.
